defects.summary: S33 reads the card's HTML through pageTree instead of running the page through runPageHtml as the plan asks, and so drops 'read off the RUNNING page;' from the exact test name; the change is recorded in §12 item 10, and the assertions do cover the Then (cooldown-line, badge and title, no reset-line with a snapshot that would draw one, the other card unchanged).

ReadResetAsync decides explicit or undecided from the reason text containing 'Individual quota reached', not from the outcome's Spent field, so a text-classified (Spent == null) agy refusal that holds the sentence is parked on stated/guess even when the gauge reads Available; this is recorded as deviation 9 but differs from D5's undecided rule.

AfterRoundAsync catches OperationCanceledException around the whole DecideAsync, so one cancelled agy probe also throws away decisions already made for other keys in the same round (for example a Claude spend-limit park).
S35 and S36 depend on a 150 ms Task.Delay so that writer B reaches the lock before A releases it; if B starts late, an unlocked implementation could still pass, so the red depends on timing.
S7 sets Attempts = 1 on the outcome itself before it calls ReviewerSummaryFactory.Describe, so the 'rate limited (after 1 attempt)' prefix is not proved for the launch as the executor returns it.

AgyError.Parse also reads pretty-printed AGY_ERROR blocks over several lines by trying to parse up to 40 growing prefixes, which goes beyond D2's 'every line starting AGY_ERROR' and is not in the §12 deviation list.

summary: Build, both suites and format are green; 42 of 43 scenarios pass under their exact names, and the 43rd (S33) is a recorded rename that still asserts its Then. D1–D11 are delivered faithfully: the structured spent verdict, the table-keyed agy groups, the /quota reader with its edge cases, the locked fail-open cooldown file with its refusal notice, per-key aggregation, roster and security-lane exclusion, the wire member and the card. The deviations are honest and recorded, and only minor findings on test timing and small spec drift remain.
